executive_summary: The 37th parliamentary session on January 29, 2026 addressed 115 topics with 108 decisions made. The meeting was dominated by intensive scrutiny of the Dutch criminal justice system's chronic case processing delays, with parliament demanding urgent structural reforms through a comprehensive 'delta plan' while the Minister of Justice advocated for incremental improvements within existing frameworks. Multiple other Justice and Security matters were debated and approved, revealing broader tensions between parliamentary oversight demands and ministerial operational autonomy.

main_topics.topic: Criminal Justice Chain Performance and Case Processing Delays
main_topics.summary: Parliament conducted an extended critical review of prolonged case processing times in the Dutch criminal justice system. Rapporteurs highlighted that despite three years of parliamentary inquiry and previous Court of Auditors warnings, visible improvements remain minimal. The current 'improvement plan' was criticized as insufficient. Key issues discussed included digitalization integration, cross-chain goal-setting, organizational culture change, and the need for clear timelines and accountability measures.

party_positions.GroenLinks-PvdA (Mutluer): Strongly critical - demands urgent, comprehensive delta plan with clear leadership, faster digitalization, and concrete timelines; argues existing improvement plan has failed to produce results over three years
party_positions.ChristenUnie (Bikker): Supportive but demanding - acknowledges good intentions but criticizes lack of concrete goals and deadlines; uses sports metaphor warning against 'knitting' instead of 'playing football'
party_positions.JA21 (Coenradie): Frustrated - questions ministerial proactivity and whether the minister is accepting unnecessary structural constraints; demands clarity on what support parliament should provide
party_positions.GroenLinks-PvdA (Ellian): Persistently demanding - notes this is the third minister on this issue with minimal progress; pushes for cultural change and cross-chain goal-setting mechanisms
party_positions.PvdA (Sneller): Assertive on accountability - points out inconsistency in treating two-year-old parliamentary motions as new exploration items
party_positions.Minister of Justice (Van Oosten): Cautiously committed - acknowledges urgency but defends current improvement plan; believes imposed delta plan inappropriate; offers increased reporting frequency (twice yearly instead of yearly) and commitment to convey parliamentary pressure to chain partners

main_topics.outcome: Minister commits to twice-yearly reporting to parliament on criminal justice improvements, will convey parliamentary urgency to the next Administrative Chain Council meeting, and will explore with chain partners whether cross-chain goals should be established. Parliament expresses dissatisfaction with pace of change but accepts minister's incremental approach pending results.

main_topics.summary: Legislative proposal for innovation law amendment was presented to parliament.

party_positions.Parliament (General): No debate required - unanimous procedural passage

main_topics.outcome: Wetsvoorstel 36784 passed without debate and without formal voting

main_topics.outcome: Minister commits to investigate whether legal definition of healthcare fraud is needed and report findings back to parliament

political_dynamics: The meeting revealed significant tension between parliamentary demands for structural reform and ministerial preference for incremental improvement within existing organizational frameworks. GroenLinks-PvdA and ChristenUnie maintained unified pressure for urgent, comprehensive action with concrete timelines and measurable goals, while the Minister of Justice resisted imposing a delta plan, arguing that stakeholder cooperation was more effective than top-down mandates. A recurring frustration emerged across multiple parties regarding the treatment of previously-passed parliamentary motions as new exploration items, suggesting concern about accountability and follow-through on ministerial commitments. JA21's questioning of ministerial proactivity indicated even center-right coalition concerns about the pace of reform. The minister's offers of increased reporting frequency appeared designed to manage parliamentary expectations while maintaining organizational autonomy, with mixed reception from rapporteurs who questioned whether more reporting without action constituted meaningful progress. No significant coalition fractures were evident, but the depth of parliamentary dissatisfaction suggests potential future motions or more forceful interventions if improvements remain slow.
